author: reek
body: EVERY REFUSAL IS EXERCISED, not just the accepting path. Each cap in the chapter is a branch that only fires on input an operator gets wrong, so an untested cap is a cap that has never run; and the failure mode of a broken cap is silent truncation, which looks exactly like a macro that worked. The table is filled to its limit here so the full-table refusal is a measurement rather than a reading of the source.

author: reek
body: REPLACEMENT IS CHECKED BY COUNT AS WELL AS BY BODY. A redefine that appended instead of replacing would still answer the new body from `macro-find` if the new entry happened to be found first, so the body alone does not discriminate; the count does.

author: reek
body: THE SIXTEENTH REDEFINE IS THE INTERESTING CASE. With the table full, a replacement must still succeed, because it does not grow the table -- checking the cap before checking whether the name exists would refuse an operator's correction on the grounds that they have made sixteen macros.
